questions.prompt: What is the chapter's main warning about talking about your ambitions too early?
choices: It can create a false sense of progress before the work exists
It always turns other people against you
It proves you have chosen the wrong goal

explanation.gentle: The problem is not every conversation. It is that recognition can arrive before contribution and weaken the pressure to work.
explanation.direct: The chapter treats early talk as emotional payoff detached from evidence.
explanation.competitive: The words can pay ego before reality does.

questions.prompt: Why does the Sherman-style anchor matter in this chapter?
choices: It proves silence is morally superior in every setting
It frames privacy as a way to keep the work from feeding on attention
It shows that leadership depends on speaking dramatically

explanation.gentle: Privacy helps because it keeps the reward tied to real effort.
explanation.direct: The anchor is about discipline, not mystique.
explanation.competitive: No audience means no cheap payment.

questions.prompt: A founder keeps announcing milestones that are not yet built and then struggles to stay focused. What is the chapter's best diagnosis?
choices: The founder needs more branding practice
Early recognition is feeding identity before contribution
The founder is talking too little to the team

explanation.gentle: The social reward is arriving before the evidence.
explanation.competitive: The image is eating the fuel that should have gone to the build.

questions.prompt: Priya hears a student group spend an hour describing how influential they will be, but no one has finished the work due tomorrow. Which move fits the chapter best?
choices: Keep the conversation inspiring so motivation stays high
Ask the room to define what still has to be delivered and by whom
Tell everyone they should never discuss goals in public again

explanation.gentle: The chapter pushes the group back toward evidence and delivery.
explanation.direct: Choice B distinguishes execution from identity talk.
explanation.competitive: If the room feels important and nothing is done, cut straight to the unfinished work.

questions.prompt: What is the important limit the chapter keeps alive?
choices: Any discussion of plans is a mistake
Useful coordination speech can help the work exist
Confidence only matters after success arrives

explanation.gentle: The chapter is not anti-communication in general.
explanation.direct: Some speech belongs when it improves execution and accountability.
explanation.competitive: Words are allowed when they sharpen the job instead of inflating the self.

questions.prompt: Why is 'never talk about your goals' a weak summary of the chapter?
choices: Because the chapter says public identity is always the fastest path to discipline
Because the chapter distinguishes execution-serving words from ego-serving words
Because the chapter is mostly about success, not ambition

explanation.gentle: The sharper line is about function, not total silence.
explanation.direct: Speech is judged by whether it advances the work or mainly rewards the self-image.
explanation.competitive: Volume is not the issue. Payment structure is.

questions.prompt: Tessa stops posting about her new routine and starts privately tracking the days completed. What changed?
choices: She moved the reward from attention to evidence
She gave up on accountability completely
She decided identity no longer matters at all

explanation.gentle: The routine now has to stand on real repetition.
explanation.direct: The payoff shifts from social response to completed effort.
explanation.competitive: She stopped feeding the costume and started feeding the proof.

questions.prompt: Which situation best shows words helping rather than replacing the work?
choices: A team keeps refining how ambitious the mission sounds
A mentor helps narrow the next execution step and set a deadline
A founder repeats the long-term vision to feel energized again

explanation.gentle: That conversation increases the chance that real effort happens next.
explanation.direct: It exposes the work to accountability and precision instead of image management.
explanation.competitive: Those words push output. The others mostly protect self-concept.

questions.prompt: What is the chapter's deeper warning about public identity formed too early?
choices: It can create a reputation the person starts maintaining before they have earned it
It guarantees the eventual work will fail
It makes ambition morally impure

explanation.gentle: The person may start protecting the image instead of testing it.
explanation.direct: A social self built from possibility creates maintenance pressure before proof exists.
explanation.competitive: Now the image has to be defended, and the work starts serving it.

questions.prompt: If words no longer count as proof of seriousness, what question does the chapter point toward next?
choices: How to become more persuasive in public
Whether ambition wants status or contribution
Why failure matters more than success

explanation.gentle: The next move is to ask what ambition should actually serve.
explanation.direct: The bridge is from false identity to the be-or-do fork.
explanation.competitive: Once display is disqualified, ambition has to choose work over status or vice versa.
